si4_title: Multiscale heterogeneity of functional connectivity in autism

dc1_datasets_using.detail: EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP); Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE-I); Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange II (ABIDE-II); total 1,824 participants pooled from 32 sites.
dc1_datasets_using.supporting_text: We pooled scans from three large datasets: the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) (Loth et al., 2017) ..., and the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchanges I and II, or ABIDE-I and ABIDE-II

dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Neurotypical (NT) participants from all three pooled datasets were used to train the normative model and establish normative ranges (with 10-fold cross-validation). Autistic participants from all datasets were used as the test group to quantify deviations from the normative baseline.
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: The normative model was trained on the group of neurotypical individuals to establish a normative range for FC and was then tested on the FC maps of the autistic individual's group ... We quantified the extent of FC deviations in the control group using 10-fold crossvalidation.
dc2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Ilioska2024.pdf.md: METHODS AND MATERIALS / Normative modeling

dc3_hc_number.detail: A total of 1028 neurotypical (NT) individuals were used as the normative population. The model was trained on the NT group, and internal evaluation was performed via 10-fold cross-validation (implying a training set of ~925 per fold, though 1028 is the total available HC N).
dc3_hc_number.supporting_text: The final sample included 796 autistic individuals (141 females; age-range: 5-58) and 1028 neuro-typical (NT) individuals (256 females; age-range: 5-56) ... The normative model was trained on the group of neurotypical individuals
